title: Node.js reading: 100,000 and 1,000,000 rows
dataset: The write benchmark's 10 columns plus a header row, written by Hypaxel with a shared string table and a reference on every cell, as Excel saves them (9.5 MB and 94 MB files)
method: benchmarks/read_bench.mjs. Single runs; each case runs in its own process and reports the non-empty cells it read, and every library returns the same cells. Peak RSS includes Node.js itself, about 81 MB.
notes: SheetJS reads the whole file into memory and is not run at 1M rows.
With inline strings instead of a shared string table, Hypaxel's peak RSS stays at 88 MB at both sizes (1.68 s for 1M rows), and ExcelJS takes 12.92 s.
The WebAssembly row runs the browser build in Node.js; it holds the file in WebAssembly memory as well as in a Buffer.
reproduce: cd node && npm run build && node benchmarks/read_bench.mjs && node benchmarks/read_bench.mjs 1000000
